newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian OTC stocks recover, weekly trade subdued.
newsitem.headline: Croatian OTC stocks recover, weekly trade subdued.

text.p: Croatian stocks began to recover last week in over-the-counter trade, tracing similar developments on the Zagreb bourse, the Varazdin securities market reported on Monday.
The activity still remained fairly subdued with turnover little changed at 3.2 million kuna, though volume rose to 9,890 from just over 8,000 units a week earlier.
The VIN index of 10 most actively traded issues regained 215 points or 1.22 percent on a weekly basis, ending last Friday at 9,813 points.
Overall, six of 24 issues rose and seven fell, while 11 closed flat. Shares in seven other firms also changed hands in direct deals between brokerages.
The biggest of six gainers was Varazdinska Banka second series preferred stock. It ended 8.80 percent higher at 1,360 kuna for the 500 kuna face value ahead of its official listing.
The bank's ordinary shares firmed 5.0 percent to 42,000 kuna -- same as their last week's price on the central bourse, though traded volume was minimal. They have a face value of 16,000 kuna each.

Both issues will be admitted to the top stock bracket of the Zagreb Stock Exchange on April 8. They are to be split and reissued with a nominal per share price of 100 kuna, pending an approval by shareholders later this month.
Insurer Croatia Osiguranje led gainers, falling 6.67 percent to 1,450 kuna.
Podravka food concern was the most active stock with 3,474 units sold. It rose 1.03 percent to end at 295 kuna -- three kuna weaker than its closing price on Zagreb's bourse.
